content_blocks.title: Practice reasoning
content_blocks.text: TF-IDF turns documents into a sparse numeric representation. The vocabulary is learned from the documents passed to fit, so place it inside cross-validation pipelines. For efficient and advanced text features, keep the problem definition, data selection, estimator configuration, and evaluation criterion explicit. When results are uncertain, compare a baseline and inspect examples rather than treating one metric as a complete explanation.

content_blocks.code:
from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import TfidfVectorizer
docs = ["refund policy", "shipping times", "refund window"]
X = TfidfVectorizer().fit_transform(docs)
print(X.shape)
print(X.nnz > 0)

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Check input shapes, target alignment, data types, missing values, label order, and whether the expected output assumes a fixed random seed. Fit learned preprocessing only on training data, preferably inside a Pipeline. Do not select parameters by repeatedly looking at the final test set.

content.task: Try it yourself: use a small synthetic or built-in dataset to practice efficient and advanced text features. State the inputs, predicted outcome, assumptions, and one limitation; compare the result with a baseline or a manually traceable expectation where appropriate.

hints: Write down inputs, expected output, and assumptions before running code.
Keep data splitting, fitting, transformation, and evaluation steps explicit; use reproducible settings when randomness is involved.

If output differs, check package versions, fixed seeds, data order, and input shapes before changing the model.

Examples use toy or built-in data; they do not establish production accuracy or business impact.
